title: Road to Modern Canada Quiz
subtitle: 80 PDF-validated multiple-choice questions from Chapters 9-11
introText: Choose the best answer. These questions focus on bold terms and content covered in Comprehension Check sections from the PDF.

questions.question: On what date did President Madison declare war in the War of 1812?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.1 asks for the date President Madison declared war.

questions.question: Which answer best explains why the United States declared war on Britain?
options: The United States wanted to control North America, and Britain was stopping trade with France
The United States wanted to join the British Empire
Britain wanted Canada to become part of France
questions.sourceNote: The War of 1812 section gives control of North America and trade with France as reasons.

questions.question: Why was the War of 1812 described as one of the most uneven wars in history?
options: Canada had far more soldiers than the United States
Only ships fought in the war
There were about 8 million Americans but only about 300,000 Canadians and 4,000 British troops in Canada
The war lasted less than one day
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.1 asks whether the war was even and why.

questions.question: What was the American invasion plan for Canada?
options: To attack only Nova Scotia by sea
To invade with General Hull at Fort Detroit and Van Rensselaer at Niagara
To wait until Canada joined the United States peacefully
To invade Alaska and move east
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.1 asks for the U.S. invasion plan.

questions.question: Which pair names the British general and the powerful Shawnee chief from section 9.1?
options: John A. Macdonald and Louis Riel
William Lyon Mackenzie and Robert E. Lee
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.1 asks for the British general and powerful Shawnee chief.

questions.question: How did Brock and Tecumseh help capture Fort Detroit?
options: They made General Hull think he faced a much larger British and Native force
They waited for Fort Detroit to run out of food for two years
They attacked only from British ships
They signed the Treaty of Ghent before the battle
questions.sourceNote: The Fort Detroit section says Brock and Tecumseh tricked General Hull into surrendering.

questions.question: What happened to General Isaac Brock at the Battle of Queenston Heights?
options: He became the first mayor of Toronto
He was shot by an American sharpshooter and died
He signed the British North America Act
He fled to the United States
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.2 connects Brock's death with Queenston Heights.

questions.question: What happened during the Burning of York?
options: Americans looted and destroyed buildings and burned Fort York
The British burned Fort Detroit by accident
questions.sourceNote: The Burning of York section describes the American attack on Fort York.

questions.question: How did Laura Secord help at Beaver Dams?
options: She wrote the Treaty of Ghent
She ran over 30 km to warn the British about an American attack
She became the first prime minister
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.2 asks how far Laura Secord ran to warn the British.

questions.question: Which treaty officially ended the War of 1812?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.2 asks which treaty ended the War of 1812.

questions.question: What did Canada gain from the War of 1812, according to the chapter?
options: A sense of unity and a strong anti-American spirit
The right to vote for women
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.2 asks what Canada gained from the War of 1812.

questions.question: The American Civil War was fought between which two sides?
options: The Union in the north and the Confederates in the south
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks which war was fought between the northern and southern states.

questions.question: What were the two main causes of the American Civil War listed in the chapter?
options: The Treaty of Ghent and Fort Detroit
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks for the two main causes of the Civil War.

questions.question: What is an abolitionist?
options: A soldier in the North-West Mounted Police
A person who hated slavery and wanted it made illegal
A leader of the Family Compact
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks students to define abolitionist.

questions.question: What was the Underground Railroad?
options: A real railway tunnel under Canada
A secret network of abolitionists helping enslaved people escape
A road from Fort Detroit to York
A train line built by the Canadian Pacific Railway
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks whether the Underground Railroad was underground or a real railroad.

questions.question: What was the goal of the Underground Railroad?
options: To help enslaved people reach freedom in the northern states and Canada
To move Mounties to the Northwest
To connect Halifax and Quebec City
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks for the goal of the Underground Railroad.

questions.question: What did the 13th Amendment do?
options: Abolished slavery in the United States
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.3 asks what the amendment did; the section explains it abolished slavery.

questions.question: What is a rebel, according to section 9.4?
options: A person who always works for the government
A person who objects to, questions, or defies existing authority
A person who builds railway tunnels
A person who donates money to the Underground Railroad
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.4 asks what a rebel is.

questions.question: Who led the Lower Canada rebellion, and what did the French-speaking reformers call themselves?
options: William Lyon Mackenzie and the Tories
John A. Macdonald and the Mounties
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.4 asks who led the Lower Canada rebellion.

questions.question: Who made the important decisions in Lower Canada before the rebellion?
options: The Chateau Clique, mainly English-speaking colonists appointed by the governor
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.4 asks who made the important decisions and who was in the group.

questions.question: What document did Papineau send with the Patriotes' demands?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.4 asks for the document sent with the Patriotes' demands.

questions.question: Where were the Patriotes finally defeated?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.4 asks where the Patriotes were finally defeated.

questions.question: Who led the Upper Canada Rebellion, and what group ruled Upper Canada?
options: William Lyon Mackenzie and the Family Compact
Isaac Brock and the Chateau Clique
Benito Mussolini and the Rome-Berlin Axis
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.5 asks for Mackenzie and the group that ruled Upper Canada.

questions.question: Where was the headquarters of the Upper Canada rebels?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 9.5 asks where the rebel headquarters was.

questions.question: Which four colonies became the Dominion of Canada on July 1, 1867?
options: Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Ontario, and Quebec
Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, and British Columbia
Upper Canada, Alaska, France, and Britain
Rupert's Land, Fort Garry, York, and Detroit
questions.sourceNote: The Confederation section names the four colonies joined by the British North America Act.

questions.question: What did John A. Macdonald purchase from the Hudson's Bay Company in 1869?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.1 asks what Macdonald purchased from the Hudson's Bay Company.

questions.question: When were the Northwest Territories officially created?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.1 asks when the Northwest Territories were officially created.

questions.question: What were people of both Native and European descent called?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.1 asks what people of Native and European descent were called.

questions.question: Who led the Red River Rebellion?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.1 asks who led the Red River Rebellion.

questions.question: What happened after Thomas Scott was executed during the Red River Rebellion?
options: Ontario demanded government action, Riel fled, and Manitoba was created in 1870
Canada immediately joined the League of Nations
The Treaty of Ghent was signed
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.1 asks what happened to Thomas Scott and when Manitoba joined Confederation.

questions.question: What was the wildest and most infamous whisky trading fort?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.2 asks for the wildest and most infamous whisky trading fort.

questions.question: What colour were the Mounties' uniforms, and when were they officially established?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.2 asks the Mountie uniform colour and establishment year.

questions.question: How much land could a settler receive through the Dominion Lands Act?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.2 asks how many acres a settler could receive.

questions.question: What did Treaty 6 promise Native people?
options: A place in the Paris Peace Conference
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.2 asks what Treaty 6 promised Native people.

questions.question: According to the chapter, did Treaty 6 recognize Native people as Canadian citizens?
options: No, it did not recognize them as Canadian citizens
Only if they joined the Mounties
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.2 asks whether Native people became citizens through Treaty 6.

questions.question: What were the Metis worried about before the Northwest Rebellion?
options: The loss of their lands and lifestyle
The end of the War of 1812
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks what the Metis were worried about.

questions.question: Why did many Native people feel cheated by the government in the Northwest?
options: The buffalo had disappeared, and promised food was poor quality
They were forced to fight at Queenston Heights
They were not allowed to ride trains
They had to pay for the Treaty of Ghent
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks why Native people felt cheated.

questions.question: Who convinced Louis Riel to return from the United States to help the Metis?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks who came back to help the Metis and identifies Dumont's role.

questions.question: Which Cree leaders joined the Metis revolt?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks for the two Cree leaders.

questions.question: What happened at Duck Lake?
options: The Metis rebels attacked the Mounties, killing 12 and forcing a retreat
The Canadian Pacific Railway was completed
Women won the right to vote in Manitoba
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks what happened at Duck Lake.

questions.question: What happened to Louis Riel after the defeat at Batoche?
options: He was tried for high treason and hanged in Regina
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.3 asks what happened to Louis Riel.

questions.question: What was a surveyor's job for railway building?
options: To discover the shortest and safest railway route
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.4 asks what a surveyor's job was.

questions.question: Which railway connected Halifax to Quebec City?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.4 asks which railway connected Halifax and Quebec City.

questions.question: What was the greatest obstacle to completing the Canadian Pacific Railway?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.4 asks for the greatest railway-building obstacle.

questions.question: Where did the east and west railway construction crews meet for the Last Spike?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.4 asks where the crews met.

questions.question: How many Chinese labourers did Andrew Onderdonk bring to Canada for railway work?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.4 asks how many Chinese labourers were brought to Canada.

questions.question: What was the main goal of residential schools?
options: To make Indigenous children live according to white customs and beliefs
To train Mounties for Fort Whoop-Up
To build the Canadian Pacific Railway
To prepare Canada for the Paris Peace Conference
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.5 asks for the main goal of residential schools.

questions.question: What were girls and boys commonly taught at residential schools?
options: Girls were taught laundry, sewing, cooking, and cleaning; boys were taught farming, carpentry, and maintenance
All students were trained as railway surveyors
Girls and boys were both taught only military strategy
All students were taught to lead the Family Compact
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.5 asks what girls and boys were taught.

questions.question: When was the last residential school closed?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.5 asks when the last residential school closed.

questions.question: When is National Day for Truth and Reconciliation?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.5 asks for National Day for Truth and Reconciliation.

questions.question: What was the Social Gospel?
options: A religious movement that wanted to solve social problems through Christian principles
A railway between Halifax and Quebec City
A treaty promising food and medical help
A secret code used by slave hunters
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.6 asks for the religious movement behind social reform.

questions.question: What is suffrage?
options: The right to vote in elections
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.6 asks what suffrage is.

questions.question: Who was the most famous and influential person for women's suffrage in this section?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.6 asks for the most famous and influential person for women's suffrage.

questions.question: Which province was the last to allow women to vote and hold office?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 10.6 asks which province was last to allow women to vote.

questions.question: How did World War I begin?
options: Archduke Franz Ferdinand was murdered by a Serbian
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks how World War I began.

questions.question: Why did Canada join World War I?
options: Canada supported Britain's decision and joined the Allied forces
Canada had been invaded by Japan
Canada was forced by the Treaty of Ghent
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks why Canada joined the war.

questions.question: How many Canadians went to fight in World War I between 1914 and 1918?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks how many Canadians went to fight in World War I.

questions.question: What happened at the Battle of Ypres in 1915?
options: Canadians held the line after Germans used poison gas
Canada signed the British North America Act
The Last Spike was hammered into place
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks about one of the worst battles Canadians fought in during World War I.

questions.question: What is conscription?
options: Forcing men to join the army
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks what conscription is.

questions.question: Why did farmers, Quakers, and Mennonites oppose conscription?
options: Farmers did not want sons taken from farms, while Quakers and Mennonites believed war was evil
They wanted Canada to join Germany
They wanted to build Fort York
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks who opposed conscription and why.

questions.question: When did World War I end?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks when World War I ended.

questions.question: Which peacekeeping force did Canada join after World War I?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks for the peacekeeping force Canada joined.

questions.question: Who wrote In Flanders Fields?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.1 asks for the poem and its writer.

questions.question: What do historians call the 1920s?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.2 asks what historians call the 1920s.

questions.question: What was the Great Depression?
options: A severe economic decline after the New York Stock Market Crash
A military alliance between Italy and Germany
A railway pass through the Rocky Mountains
A treaty that ended the War of 1812
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.2 asks what the Great Depression was.

questions.question: What percent of the population did not have jobs by 1933?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.2 asks what percent of the population did not have jobs.

questions.question: What did Alberta and Saskatchewan suffer from during the Great Depression?
options: A severe drought that led to crop failure
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.2 asks what Alberta and Saskatchewan suffered from.

questions.question: Which two famous Canadian companies were started during the Great Depression?
options: Hudson's Bay Company and Northwest Company
Canadian Pacific Railway and Intercolonial Railway
Salvation Army and League of Nations
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.2 asks which famous Canadian companies started in the 1930s.

questions.question: Who was the leader of Italy before World War II?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks who led Italy.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Treaty of Versailles, according to the chapter?
options: To prevent Germany from ever starting another war
To create the Dominion of Canada
To end the Red River Rebellion
To give women the right to vote
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks for the purpose of the Treaty of Versailles.

questions.question: Who became the dictator of Germany?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks who led Germany.

questions.question: What area did Hitler march his soldiers back into in 1936, breaking the Treaty of Versailles?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks which area Germany marched soldiers back into.

questions.question: Who was part of the Rome-Berlin Axis?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks who was part of the Rome-Berlin Axis.

questions.question: After Germany invaded which country did Britain and France declare war on Germany?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks what country Germany invaded before Britain and France declared war.

questions.question: When did Canada officially declare war in World War II?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks when Canada officially declared war.

questions.question: In which battle were 907 Canadian soldiers killed, more than 500 wounded, and almost 2,000 captured?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks for the battle with these Canadian losses.

questions.question: What place did Japanese warplanes bomb on December 7, 1941?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks what place Japan bombed on December 7, 1941.

questions.question: What was Operation D-Day?
options: The Allied invasion to take back Europe from Germany
The signing of the British North America Act
The first National Day for Truth and Reconciliation
The founding of the Salvation Army
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks for the Allied invasion to take back Europe.

questions.question: What is VE Day?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks what VE Day is.

questions.question: Which two Japanese cities were attacked with atomic bombs by the United States?
questions.sourceNote: Comprehension Check 11.3 asks which two Japanese cities were attacked.
